title: Book 8 — Urania, Chapter 25
paragraphs: When the herald had made this proclamation, boats became the most sought-after thing of all, so many were those who wished to see the spectacle. When they had crossed over, they walked among the dead bodies and looked at them. Everyone supposed that those lying there were all Lacedaemonians or Thespians, though Helots too were among those they saw. Still, those who had crossed over did not fail to perceive what Xerxes had done with the bodies of his own dead — for truly it was a thing to provoke laughter: on one side lay a thousand dead bodies in view, while the others, four thousand of them, were all gathered together in one place. Throughout that day they busied themselves with viewing, and the following day they sailed back to the ships at Histaia, while Xerxes and his army set out on their march.
